== deviceConnect support for Linux hosts with Android devices

deviceConnect now runs on Linux hosts for Android devices. Organizations that host dedicated Android devices can use a Linux x64 machine as the deviceConnect host instead of a Mac mini.

Linux hosts support Android devices only. iOS devices continue to require a Mac mini host.

For host requirements, see xref:device-lab-management:deviceConnect/hardware-requirements-for-deviceconnect.adoc[].

== Improved Test Case validation and Scriptless Test Run errors

Test Management now identifies Test Cases that cannot be replayed before a Test Run starts. The *Run* option is disabled for these Test Cases, with guidance on how to record them again.

Test Cases that cannot be replayed are also excluded from Test Run and Test Suite selection. API and MCP requests return an error explaining why the Test Case cannot run, and Test Case API responses include the new `run_blocked_reason` field.

Scriptless Test Runs now report specific initialization errors and end unsuccessful attempts sooner, rather than repeatedly retrying and returning the generic `Device retry exceeded` error.

For details, see xref:test-management:test-cases.adoc#_test_cases_that_cant_run[Test Cases that can't run].

// Source: KOB-55539 from PR #854
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/854

== Improved reliability for Appium automation sessions

An unresponsive session no longer disrupts other automation sessions or prevents new sessions from starting.

Appium and REST API requests to sessions that cannot respond now return an error instead of waiting indefinitely.

// Source: KOB-55565 from PR #853
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/853

== Separate text and vision model settings for Appium AI

The *Appium AI Configuration* form now supports separate text and vision model settings.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-org-settings.adoc[Configure Appium AI settings for your organization].

== Turbo Test

// Source: KOB-55558 from PR #844
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/844

=== Retry guidance when test executors are busy

Kobiton can now limit how many Appium Turbo Test sessions each test executor runs at the same time. This keeps a burst of new sessions from overloading test executors.

When every test executor is at its limit:

- *Immediate execution mode:* `POST /v2/sessions/native` returns HTTP `503` with the message `All test executors are busy. Please retry later.` The device booked for the request is released. Retry the request later.
- *Queued execution mode:* Kobiton retries the test automatically until a test executor is available or `device_wait_timeout` is reached.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:turbo-test-execution/run-appium-test.adoc#_handle_busy_test_executors[Handle busy test executors].

// Source: KOB-55559 from PR #859
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/859

=== Sessions continue during infrastructure scaling and updates

Appium Turbo Test sessions that are running when Kobiton scales down or updates its test execution infrastructure now run to completion instead of being terminated. Results and test reports from these sessions remain available as usual.

During these events, new Turbo Test sessions start on other available infrastructure.

// Source: KOB-55678 from PR #839
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/839

=== Device still reserved by a previous session

Fixed an issue where starting a Turbo Test session on a specific device with `POST /v2/sessions/native` returned an HTTP 500 error when your previous Turbo Test session still held that device. While the device remains reserved, the request now returns HTTP 404 with the message `No device available.` Retry the request after the device is released. Queued sessions record the 404 response instead of a server error and continue to retry as before.

// Source: KOB-55674 from PR #828
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/828

=== Faster recovery from connection interruptions

Turbo Test now detects an interrupted connection and reconnects automatically, so new sessions resume processing sooner.

Previously, an interrupted connection could pause the processing of new Turbo Test sessions, and sessions started during that time could fail with a timeout error.

When a connection is interrupted:

- Sessions that are already running continue, complete, and upload their test reports.
- Sessions that have not finished starting are canceled and retried automatically.

// Source: KOB-54805 from PR #835
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/835

== More predictable responses from MCP tools

- The `terminateSession` MCP tool now returns a successful result with status `already_ended` when the session has already ended. Previously, this call returned an error. An unknown session ID still returns an error.
- The `saveTestCase` MCP tool now returns a retryable error with the code `SESSION_PROCESSING` and a `retry_after_sec` value when the session is still being processed after it ends. Previously, it returned an error with no explanation. Wait the indicated number of seconds, then retry the call.
- The `getCredential` MCP tool now returns a successful result for MCP clients that authenticate with a static API-key header. Previously, these calls returned a `401 Unauthorized` error.

// Source: KOB-55629 from PR #830
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/830

== Remove files from devices with Kobiton CLI

The new `kobiton file rm` command removes a file or an empty folder from an Android or iOS device in a CLI session.

- A successful removal prints `Removed <path>` and exits `0`.
- A removal fails with a non-zero exit status when the path does not exist or the folder still contains files.

For details, see xref:kobiton-cli:cli-commands.adoc#file-rm[`file rm`].

// Source: KOB-55695 from PR #851
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/851

=== MTBF report loads for large device fleets

Fixed an issue where the *Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF)* report could fail to load and display an error instead of the chart for organizations with a large number of devices.

== Known issues with fold and unfold in manual sessions

- After a fold or unfold, the saved session video can appear stretched or distorted.
- In Session Explorer, *Inspector* can be misaligned on steps captured after a fold or unfold.

== Accurate colors in Lightning mode on Android devices

Lightning mode now displays accurate colors on Android devices.

Previously, red and blue could appear swapped in the Lightning mode video on some Android devices. For example, blue icons appeared orange. Screenshots in Session Explorer were not affected.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55660): The fix passed internal regression testing, but the original symptom was not reproduced in the lab, and verification on the affected devices is still pending. Confirm resolution before publishing.

// Source: KOB-55417 from PR #856
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/856

== Read device identifiers in automation scripts

Appium automation sessions now support the `mobile: deviceIdentifiers` command, which returns the advertising and tracking identifiers a device holds. Use it to compare the identifiers your app reports with the values on the device.

* *Advertising ID:* Read the IDFA on iOS and the AAID on Android. On iOS, the response also includes the app tracking status.
* *Android ID:* Read the Android ID (SSAID) along with the signing certificate it belongs to.
* *DRM ID:* Read the DRM ID of an Android app that is a debug build and is running.

The identifier for vendor (IDFV) on iOS is not supported.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:scripting/read-device-identifiers-in-appium-script.adoc[].

// Source: KOB-55513 from PR #849
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/849

== Improved page source reliability during Android screen transitions

Appium page source requests on Android devices no longer intermittently fail while an app screen opens or closes.

Previously, finding an element by XPath immediately after opening a screen or pressing *Back* could return `SessionException: Agent error: GET /system/inventory, node_access_error ()`.

When the app window is briefly unavailable during a screen transition, page source requests now retry for up to 1 second before returning an error. The improvement also applies to the view hierarchy that manual sessions capture after each action.

On screens that display only system windows, such as the lock screen or an expanded notification shade, page source requests still return `node_access_error`.

// Source: KOB-54746 from PR #848
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/848

=== TalkBack Enhanced keymap

Fixed an issue where the *Screen Reader* panel buttons, such as *Next* and *Previous*, did not move the TalkBack focus on Android devices that use the Enhanced keymap introduced in TalkBack 16.2. The buttons now work with both the Default and Enhanced keymaps. Switching the device back to the Default keymap is no longer required.

// Source: KOB-55682 from PR #841
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/841

=== Jetpack Compose screens on Android

Fixed an issue where the *Inspector* XML hierarchy was missing content on Android 13 and later for Jetpack Compose screens that contain native Android views. The hierarchy showed only elements such as the status bar and the bottom navigation, and the rest of the screen appeared as empty `android.view.View` elements with no text or resource ID. These screens now show their full content in the hierarchy.

// Source: KOB-54826 from PR #825
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/825

== Session videos on long-running deviceConnect hosts

Fixed an issue where sessions on a deviceConnect host stopped producing session videos after the host's video capture service had been running for an extended period. Sessions started and live view worked normally, but no video was available on the session detail page after the session ended. The issue affected every device on the host until the video capture service restarted.

// Source: KOB-52316 from PR #824
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/824

== Lightning Mode fix for some Android devices

Fixed an issue where Lightning Mode failed to start on some Android devices, such as the Samsung Galaxy Tab A9+, whose video encoder does not support the device's full screen resolution. On these devices, Lightning Mode now streams at a lower resolution than the device's screen. Other devices continue to stream at the same resolution as before.
